chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muyassir ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'O Muyassir! Supplicate and do not say that the matter has already been decided. Indeed, with God — Mighty and Majestic — there is a station that cannot be attained except by asking. And if a servant were to close his mouth and not ask, he would not be given anything. So ask, and you will be given. O Muyassir! There is no door that is knocked upon except that it is about to be opened for the one who knocks.'

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ قَدْ فُرِغَ مِنْهُ: The matter has been decided — a fatalistic expression implying that God's decree is fixed and supplication cannot change it; the Imam rejects using this as an excuse to abandon du'a
key_terms.بِمَسْأَلَة: By asking/supplication — the specific mechanism by which certain divine blessings are unlocked; not merely recommended but required
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God expressing His power and grandeur, used frequently in hadith literature
key_terms.مَنْزِلَة: Station/rank in the divine presence — a spiritual status or blessing that God reserves for those who ask; emphasizes the instrumentality of supplication in the divine economy

ai.seo_question: Does God's predetermination make supplication (du'a) pointless in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) directly exhorts his companion Muyassir ibn Abd al-Aziz to persist in supplication and reject the fatalistic notion that divine predetermination makes du'a pointless. The Imam teaches that God has reserved certain blessings that can only be obtained through asking, making supplication not merely recommended but a prerequisite for receiving divine bounty. This hadith addresses a theological misunderstanding common in early Islamic thought: that if God has already decreed everything, supplication is futile — the Imam corrects this by affirming that asking is itself part of the divine plan and a condition for receiving.
word_analysis: for its owner/the one who knocks

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muyassir Bin Abdul Aziz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>

said to me: ‘O Muyassir! Supplicate and do not say that the matter has already been decided. In the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Might and Majestic there is a status which cannot be achieved except by asking (for it), and if a servant was to close his mouth and not ask, he would not be Given a thing. Therefore ask, you will be Given. O Muyassir! There is no door which is knocked upon except it is imminent that it would be opened for its comer’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Maysir ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once said to me, ‘O Maysir, pray and do not say that it is predetermined and it is all over. There is a position with Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, that is not accessible without praying to Him. If a servant keeps his mouth closed and does not plead to receive help, he will not receive anything. O Maysir, there is no door that is knocked repeatedly but that sooner or later it will open up.’”
